prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Reform UK Manifesto 2024 – Summary (≤500 words)

Premise
Reform UK argues Britain has been damaged by high taxes, debt, mass immigration, “woke” ideology, Net Zero policies, weak borders, crime, and public service failures. It proposes “common sense” reforms to restore sovereignty, cut waste, lower taxes, and prioritise British culture and values.

Five core pledges
- Freeze non-essential immigration and stop small boats.
- Zero NHS waiting lists while keeping care free at point of use.
- Raise the income tax threshold to £20,000 to “make work pay.”
- Scrap Net Zero and green levies to cut energy bills and expand domestic oil and gas.
- Restore law and order and cut government waste.

Key policies by area
- Immigration: Freeze non-essential visas; leave ECHR; create a Department of Immigration; return small boats to France; detain and offshore-process illegal arrivals; bar asylum from safe countries; deport foreign criminals; bar student dependants; five-year residency/work for benefits; impose a higher employer NI rate (20%) for foreign workers, exempting essential health/care and micro-firms.
- Government waste: Stop paying interest on QE reserves; cut 5% “waste” across departments; deregulate post-Brexit; halve foreign aid; improve HMRC tax collection.
- Personal economy: Lift income tax start point to £20k; higher rate from £70k; cut fuel duty by 20p; scrap VAT on energy and environmental levies; cut stamp duty (0% to £750k); restore VAT-free tourist shopping; raise IHT threshold to £2m (20% above, with charity option).
- Business: Raise corporation tax threshold to £100k; cut main rate to 20%, then 15% by year 3; abolish IR35; lift VAT threshold to £150k; abolish business rates for high street SMEs, offset by a 4% online delivery tax; planning and deregulation reforms; simplify the tax code.
- NHS: Zero basic rate tax for NHS/social care staff for 3 years; expand UK training and write off fees via service; use independent capacity (UK/overseas); 20% tax relief on private healthcare/insurance; voucher guarantees for GP, consultant, and operation waits; efficiency drives; “Pharmacy First”; inquiry into excess deaths/vaccine harms.
- Energy/Net Zero: Scrap Net Zero and subsidies; fast-track North Sea oil/gas and shale pilots; expand nuclear SMRs; support domestic lithium, gas turbines, tidal, and other tech.
- Policing/Justice: +40,000 officers; zero-tolerance, expanded stop and search; tougher drug and knife crime penalties; end “woke”/DEI roles; redefine hate crime; expand prison places; faster courts.
- Education: “Patriotic curriculum”; ban transgender ideology in schools; 20% tax relief on independent schooling; scrap interest on student loans and extend repayment to 45 years; tougher university standards; protect free speech; more PRUs for exclusions.
- Benefits: Stricter conditionality (job within 4 months or after 2 offers); face-to-face assessments; focus on youth employment.
- Brexit/Constitution: Scrap remaining EU laws; abandon Windsor Framework; PR referendum; leave ECHR; reform House of Lords and Civil Service; tighten postal voting; British Bill of Rights.
- Defence: Raise spending to 2.5% of GDP by year 3, 3% by year 6; pay rises; legal protections for personnel; new veterans department; recruit 30,000 for the Army; procurement reform.
- Housing: Fast-track brownfield; prioritise locals for social housing; restore landlord mortgage interest relief; drop Renters’ Reform Bill; strengthen leaseholder rights.
- Families: Transferable marriage tax allowance (25%); front-load child benefit ages 1–4; single-sex spaces; address social media harms.
- Transport/Infrastructure: Scrap HS2; ban ULEZ/LTNs; accelerate regional road/rail; new 50/50 utility ownership (state/pension funds); cap standing charges.
- Agriculture/Fisheries: More farm support; scrap climate-linked subsidies; protect country sports; curb EU fishing access; expand patrols; ban supertrawlers; rebuild processing.
- Elderly/Social Care: Royal Commission; curb tax avoidance by large care chains; pension reforms; mineworkers’ pension fix.
- Culture/“Reclaiming Britain”: Reject WEF/WHO treaty/CBDC; replace Equalities Act; free speech bill; reform BBC and scrap licence fee; new national holidays; anti-corruption unit.

Funding (claimed)
Annual savings/growth: ~£160bn (waste cuts, Net Zero rollback, benefits, immigration tax, growth). Annual costs: ~£141bn. Reform UK says this funds its programme.
